description: Extract document file content (real text extraction -- pdfplumber/python-docx/BeautifulSoup) from cloud storage and file-sharing providers for RAG pipelines. Generic bucket storage (s3/gcs/azure_blob/webdav) walks the source via fsspec; OAuth-protected vendor APIs (onedrive/sharepoint/box/dropbox) authenticate and list files the same way this repo's onedrive_ingestion/sharepoint_ingestion/box_ingestion/dropbox_ingestion components do, then fetch + extract each file's content. Every row carries the shared document source contract (doc_id, content, title, url, source_type, updated_at, content_hash) so document_chunker and other RAG components can treat every provider identically.
summary: Extract real document content from cloud storage / file-sharing providers (s3, gcs, azure, webdav, onedrive, sharepoint, box, dropbox) for RAG.
name: Cloud Documents

outputs.description: pandas DataFrame with one row per extracted document (or MaterializeResult if destination is non-SQL / persist_only=true).

asset_name.label: Asset Name
asset_name.description: Name of the asset that will hold the data

provider.label: Provider
provider.description: Which cloud storage / file-sharing provider to read from. 's3'/'gcs'/'azure_blob'/'webdav' walk a bucket/share via fsspec (source_path); 'onedrive'/'sharepoint'/'box'/'dropbox' authenticate to that vendor's own API, mirroring this repo's onedrive_ingestion/sharepoint_ingestion/box_ingestion/dropbox_ingestion components.

source_path.label: Source Path
source_path.description: Required for provider='s3'/'gcs'/'azure_blob': an fsspec URI to walk recursively (e.g. 's3://bucket/docs/', 'gs://bucket/docs/', 'az://container/docs/') -- install the matching backend (s3fs / gcsfs / adlfs). Credentials are resolved by that backend from its own standard environment variables (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY for s3fs) -- there is no separate credentials field here, matching document_ingestion's own source_path. For provider='webdav', this is instead a path RELATIVE to webdav_base_url (e.g. '/Documents/'); defaults to '/' (the share root) if unset. Ignored for onedrive/sharepoint/box/dropbox, which use their own listing fields below.

webdav_base_url.label: Webdav Base Url
webdav_base_url.description: Required when provider='webdav': the WebDAV server/share root, e.g. 'https://dav.example.com/remote.php/dav/files/user/'. Routes through fsspec's 'webdav' protocol, which this environment's fsspec already knows how to resolve to the webdav4 package (`fsspec.get_filesystem_class('webdav')` reports 'Install webdav4 to access WebDAV' rather than an unknown-protocol error) -- but webdav4 itself (pip install webdav4) is NOT installed here, so this path is best-effort / unverified end-to-end in this repo; install webdav4 and test against your own WebDAV server before relying on it in production.

webdav_username.label: Webdav Username
webdav_username.description: WebDAV basic-auth username. Pairs with webdav_password_env_var. Optional if your WebDAV server allows anonymous/token-only access.

webdav_password_env_var.label: Webdav Password Env Var
webdav_password_env_var.description: Env var holding the WebDAV basic-auth password, resolved via dagster.EnvVar. Pairs with webdav_username.

webdav_token_env_var.label: Webdav Token Env Var
webdav_token_env_var.description: Alternative to username/password: env var holding a bearer token, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', for WebDAV servers that support token auth.

tenant_id.label: Tenant Id
tenant_id.description: Required for provider='onedrive'/'sharepoint': Azure AD (Entra ID) tenant ID. Mirrors onedrive_ingestion's own `tenant_id` field name.

client_id.label: Client Id
client_id.description: Required for provider='onedrive'/'sharepoint'/'box'/'dropbox': the OAuth app's client ID. Shared across these 4 branches (each is a different vendor's app registration, but all 4 already name this field `client_id` in onedrive_ingestion/box_ingestion/dropbox_ingestion). For onedrive/sharepoint: an Azure AD app registration (Files.Read.All or Sites.Read.All application permission, admin-consented). For box: a Box app configured for Client Credentials Grant. For dropbox: a Dropbox app (used for the refresh-token exchange).

client_secret.label: Client Secret
client_secret.description: Required alongside client_id for onedrive/sharepoint/box/dropbox -- the matching OAuth app client secret.

drive_id.label: Drive Id
drive_id.description: Required for provider='onedrive': target drive ID (a user's OneDrive or a SharePoint document library's drive ID). Mirrors onedrive_ingestion's own `drive_id` field exactly.

site_hostname.label: Site Hostname
site_hostname.description: Required for provider='sharepoint': SharePoint site collection hostname, e.g. 'contoso.sharepoint.com'. Mirrors sharepoint_ingestion's own field name.

site_path.label: Site Path
site_path.description: Required for provider='sharepoint': server-relative path to the site, e.g. '/sites/TeamSite'. Combined with site_hostname to resolve the site, then its default document library drive, via two Graph calls (GET /sites/{hostname}:/{path} then GET /sites/{site-id}/drive) -- same two-call resolution sharepoint_ingestion already does.

box_subject_type.label: Box Subject Type
box_subject_type.description: Required for provider='box': Box CCG subject type, 'enterprise' or 'user'. Mirrors box_ingestion's own field name.

box_subject_id.label: Box Subject Id
box_subject_id.description: Required for provider='box': Box enterprise ID (if subject_type=enterprise) or user ID (if subject_type=user). Mirrors box_ingestion's own field name.

folder_id.label: Folder Id
folder_id.description: provider='box' only: Box folder ID to list children of. Defaults to '0' (root) if unset. Root children only -- no recursion into subfolders.

refresh_token.label: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: Required for provider='dropbox': OAuth2 refresh token obtained once via Dropbox's OAuth consent flow (token_access_type=offline) -- Dropbox deprecated long-lived static access tokens. Mirrors dropbox_ingestion's own field name.

folder_path.label: Folder Path
folder_path.description: provider='dropbox' only: Dropbox folder path to list, e.g. '/Reports'. Empty string (default) lists the root.

recursive.label: Recursive
recursive.description: provider='dropbox' only: list all nested subfolders' contents too (Dropbox's own `recursive` list_folder parameter), not just the immediate folder. Unlike onedrive/sharepoint/box, Dropbox's list_folder API supports this natively.

hash_columns.label: Hash Columns
hash_columns.description: Column names to pseudonymize (salted SHA-256, hex-encoded) before the data reaches the destination -- same deterministic-hashing pattern dlt's own docs recommend for PII (https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/customising-pipelines/pseudonymizing_columns). A column missing from a given row is skipped, not an error. Requires hash_salt or hash_salt_env_var.

hash_salt.label: Hash Salt
hash_salt.description: Salt for hash_columns. Required (this or hash_salt_env_var) when hash_columns is set -- a hardcoded/shared salt would let the hash be reversed by dictionary attack on common values. Use "{{ env.VAR_NAME }}" for the inline form. Keep it stable across runs: changing it changes every hash.

hash_salt_env_var.label: Hash Salt Env Var
hash_salt_env_var.description: Alternative to hash_salt: name of an env var holding the salt. Resolved at run-time.

on_schema_change.label: On Schema Change
on_schema_change.description: What to do when incoming data's shape differs from the destination table's established schema (new columns, or a column's data type changing). 'allow_all' (default, today's behavior): accept any change. 'allow_new_columns': accept new columns, but reject (fail the run) a column whose data type would change. 'block_all': reject both new columns and data type changes. The first materialization can always create its initial schema in every mode -- 'block_all' only locks down an ALREADY-established table's columns/types. A rejected change fails the run with a clear error naming the table and column -- it is never silently dropped.

exclude_columns.label: Exclude Columns
exclude_columns.description: Column names to drop from every row before it reaches the destination. Applied before hash_columns (so a column in both ends up excluded, not hashed-then-excluded). A column missing from a given row is skipped, not an error, matching hash_columns.

max_rows_per_resource.label: Max Rows Per Resource
max_rows_per_resource.description: Caps how many document rows load into the destination. Unset (default): no cap. This still loads real rows into the real destination -- it is not a dry run or a preview -- meant for a first run to check a connection and the shape of the data cheaply, not for routine use. Never applied unless you set it.

destination.label: Destination
destination.description: dlt destination identifier (e.g. 'snowflake', 'bigquery', 'postgres', 'redshift', 'filesystem', 'duckdb', 'databricks', 'athena', 'clickhouse', 'mssql', 'motherduck'). Leave empty for in-memory DuckDB -> DataFrame mode. This is where the extracted document ROWS this component produces get loaded -- entirely separate from the cloud source being read from (source_path / the OAuth provider's own folder/drive/site fields above).

dataset_name.label: Dataset Name
dataset_name.description: Target dataset/schema in the destination. Defaults to the asset name.

persist_only.label: Persist Only
persist_only.description: If True with destination set: emit a MaterializeResult and skip DataFrame return. If False: query the destination back into a DataFrame (only meaningful for SQL destinations -- non-SQL destinations always emit MaterializeResult).

destination_credentials_url.label: Destination Credentials Url
destination_credentials_url.description: Inline connection string passed to dlt's destination factory. Useful when one Dagster project ingests into multiple accounts of the same destination type. If unset, dlt resolves credentials from env vars -- see ../DESTINATIONS.md.

destination_credentials_env_var.label: Destination Credentials Env Var
destination_credentials_env_var.description: Alternative to destination_credentials_url: name of an env var holding the connection string. Resolved at run-time.

bucket_url.label: Bucket Url
bucket_url.description: Bucket/path URL for filesystem-shaped DESTINATION storage (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/path', 'gs://my-bucket/path', 'az://my-container/path', or 'file:///local/path'). Required when destination='filesystem' (the final write target). Also used as the staging area when destination='databricks' or 'athena'. This is NOT the same as source_path -- bucket_url is where dlt writes the output document rows; source_path is where this component reads documents FROM. dlt resolves the bucket's credentials from the destination-appropriate standard environment variables unless destination_credentials_url/destination_credentials_env_var is set.

athena_query_result_bucket.label: Athena Query Result Bucket
athena_query_result_bucket.description: Optional S3 path where Athena writes query results (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/results/'). Only used when destination='athena'. May be omitted to use Athena-managed query results instead.

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)

freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule

include_preview_metadata.label: Include Preview Metadata
include_preview_metadata.description: Include sample data preview in metadata

preview_rows.label: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: Rows to include in the preview metadata when `include_preview_metadata` is True. For long DataFrames (>10x preview_rows), a random sample is used so the preview reflects the data distribution; otherwise head() is used.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

partition_type.description: Enable partitioning: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly' for time-based; 'static' for a fixed set of values (e.g. customers); 'multi' for date × static (e.g. day × customer). Leave empty for unpartitioned.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

partition_start.description: ISO date string for the first partition, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required for time-based and multi partition types.
partition_start.label: Partition Start Date

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme_corp,globex,initech'. Required for static and multi types.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.
partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill strategy for a partitioned asset. 'single_run' materializes a whole backfill range in one run (rows are filtered to the whole range); 'multi_run' launches one run per partition, optionally capped by backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run. Unset keeps Dagster's default. Needs a partition-range-aware IO manager for single_run.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Policy Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For backfill_policy='multi_run' only: maximum partitions materialized per run (default 1).

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

column_lineage.label: Column Lineage
column_lineage.description: Column-level lineage, emitted as `dagster/column_lineage` metadata on every materialization: {output column: [upstream columns]}, e.g. {'chunk_text': ['content']}. The upstream asset is `upstream_asset_key`, or the only entry of `deps`; with several upstream assets, name each column '<asset_key>:<column>'. Ignored with a warning when no upstream asset can be resolved.

partition_date_column.description: Column used to filter the returned DataFrame to the current date partition (time partitions).
partition_date_column.label: Partition Date Column

partition_static_column.description: Column used to filter the returned DataFrame to the current static/dynamic partition key.
partition_static_column.label: Partition Static Column

storage_options_env_vars.label: Storage Options Env Vars
storage_options_env_vars.description: Only used for provider='s3'/'gcs'/'azure_blob'. Maps an fsspec storage_option key to the env var name holding its value, e.g. {'endpoint_url': 'S3_ENDPOINT_URL'} for an S3-compatible endpoint (Cloudflare R2, MinIO, Rustfs, ...), or {'key': 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID', 'secret': 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'} to override s3fs's own ambient credential chain explicitly. Resolved via dg.EnvVar at materialization time only -- never baked into the code location at load time. Omit to keep using fsspec's ambient auth (the cloud SDK's own default credential chain), which already works for real S3/GCS/Azure without this field.
